Missing data never closes a fire. (b) BASIS CLAUSE: an exit may be taken ONLY on the SINGLE-SOURCE basis (fill AND 5-yr norm both AGSI-derived). column7: ORANGE FIRE OPEN, now on a SINGLE-SOURCE basis. 🔴 2026-09-19 RE-BASED TO SINGLE-SOURCE AFTER THE AGSI KEY LANDED. Gap -15.99pp = AGSI fill 69.06% [gas day 2026-09-17] minus an AGSI-NATIVE 5-yr norm of 85.05% (mean of the SAME gas day 09-17 across 2021-2025: 71.26/85.67/93.87/93.38/81.09; median 85.67 gives -16.61pp, so the verdict is robust to the central measure). ⛔ THE MOVE FROM -19.7 TO -15.99 IS A BASIS CORRECTION, NOT A STORAGE RECOVERY. Decomposition: fill contributed +0.76pp (68.3 -> 69.06), the NORM contributed +2.95pp (88.0 -> 85.05) - ~80% of the change is the denominator. Do NOT report this as improvement. 🔴 AND THE SCRIPT'S OWN NORM WAS WORSE: fetch_eu.py carried a HARDCODED 82.0 frozen on 2026-08-28 and applied to every later date, which printed -12.9pp today. Two defects in one constant: cross-source, AND frozen-seasonal - the true norm RISES through the injection season, so a frozen constant makes the gap read BETTER as time passes. THAT IS FAIL-OPEN DRIFT, the one direction a storage alarm must never fail in. It had the fire on the wrong side of its own -15 band. Fixed: agsi_norm() now computes the norm from AGSI history, fail-closed (no norm => NO GAP PRINTED, never a constant fallback). ✅ FIRE STAYS OPEN at -15.99 (band <=-15), by 0.99pp on the mean basis and 1.61pp on the median. The exit clause registered this morning did its job on its first live pull: had I accepted the cross-source -12.9 the row would have looked 2.1pp from an exit on a norm AGSI's own history contradicts.
